newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Foreign investment dips 35 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Foreign investment dips 35 pct in March.

text.p: Foreign investment inflows into Colombia fell 35 percent to $107 million in March compared to the same month last year, mixed-capital investment corporation Coinvertir said Tuesday.
Levels were hit especially by cuts in investment in the mining and quarrying sector, Coinvertir said.
It is the second consecutive monthly fall after foreign investment fell 6.6 percent in February.
According to statistics released by the corporation foreign investment inflows in the first quarter of this year were up 29 percent to $419 million compared to the same period in 1996.
Coinvertir said 61 percent of foreign investment in March was destined toward manufacturing industry and 29 percent toward the finance and insurance sector.
In the first quarter a total of $134 million of foreign investment was pumped into manufacturing, with $75 million in transport and storage and $43 million to the business sector, Coinvertir said.

The United States maintained its position at the head of the foreign investment league table with $146 million, or 35 percent of the total, in the first quarter, followed by the Virgin Islands with $46 million.
